subject: Post-demo follow-up — privacy/dataflow questions & proposed next steps
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medsys.io>, Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@medsys.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T09:15:00-05:00
Subject: Post-demo follow-up — privacy/dataflow questions & proposed next steps

Thanks again for your time this morning — appreciate the detailed walkthrough and the context on the telemetry/PHI handling requirements at MedSys. Per our call, I wanted to summarize the open privacy items and propose a short mutual action plan so legal and security teams have what they need to evaluate Redwood for the pilot.

Open items we flagged on the call:
1) Data flows — please confirm which of the three flows below are in scope for the pilot: API-only (no log retention), API + KV cache (short-lived), or API + long-term persistence for indexing. We attached a short summary of Redwood defaults (Redwood_DPA_Summary_20261122.pdf).
2) Controller vs Processor — quick confirmation that MedSys will require a DPA that lists MedSys as Controller and Redwood as Processor, and whether you need any bespoke language around model outputs/derivatives.
3) Subprocessors — request for our subprocessor registry and whether advance notification (vs. notice-after) is required.
4) Breach notification SLA — you asked about timelines; please confirm whether 48 hours is acceptable or if you need 24/72.
5) Data residency — confirm EU-only residency requirement (we can pin to eu-west-1 for Dedicated/Private).
6) Logging/access controls — scope of audit logs you need (access logs, token-level, admin console access).
7) Retention & deletion — default token/log retention and options to shorten or purge on request.

Suggested next steps (proposed MAP):
- Legal: exchange DPA drafts; Redwood will provide a redlineable DPA and subprocessor registry link by EOD.
- Security: we can run a short architecture call (30m) to walk data flows and logging configuration — propose Tue 11/24 or Wed 11/25.
- Pilot: confirm which data flow mode you want for the 6-week pilot so we can provision appropriately.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Summary_20261122.pdf (summary, not full DPA).

If that reflects your notes, can you confirm preferred breach-notify SLA and local residency requirement? Happy to coordinate a quick call with Ben (legal) and Marissa (solutions) tomorrow.

Best,
Vivek
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Dr. Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medsys.io>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@medsys.io>
Date: 2026-11-22T12:02:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up — privacy/dataflow questions & proposed next steps

Hi Vivek — thanks, that summary is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- MedSys will act as Controller for clinical data. We expect the vendor to be Processor. We are especially interested in confirming whether model-derived artifacts (summaries/embeddings) will be treated as processed personal data and whether Redwood persists those by default.
- For the pilot we want API-only with no persistent index; KV cache for session responsiveness is acceptable if it can be scoped to 24 hours and disabled for PHI endpoints.
- Subprocessors: our procurement team prefers advance notification for any new subprocessor that will handle PHI. Is that feasible?
- Breach timeline: our internal target is notification within 72 hours for any confirmed data breach impacting PHI, with ongoing updates. Would Redwood accept 72h (rather than 48)?
- Residency: EU-only (eu-west-1) is a strict requirement for this project.
- Logging: we need token-level access logs and an audit trail of admin console actions for the pilot (90-day retention, searchable).

I have attached our privacy checklist (MedSys_PrivChecklist.xlsx) — it lists mandatory clauses they will expect in the final DPA. If you can provide the subprocessor registry URL and a SOC2 report snapshot, that would accelerate review.

Thanks — available for a 30m call tomorrow afternoon CET if that helps.

Regards,
Dr. Elena Rossi
Chief Data Officer, MedSys Health
elena.rossi@medsys.io

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medsys.io>, Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@medsys.io>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T14:10:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up — privacy/dataflow questions & proposed next steps

Elena/Carlos — quick note from legal to address the points above. Appreciate the checklist — that helps.

Controller/Processor: Redwood's standard posture is that customers are Controllers and Redwood acts as Processor for customer data provided in API requests. Model outputs are considered processed outputs; by default we do not persist outputs beyond what is required for the request, unless explicitly configured for indexing or analytics. We'll add explicit language around derivatives in the DPA redline.

Subprocessors: we maintain a live registry at https://app.redwood.ai/subprocessors and we can provide an export for procurement. Our standard is notice-after for standard infra subprocessors; for vendors that will materially process PHI we can agree to advance notice and a 30-day review window as part of enterprise terms.

Logging & retention: default request logs and token traces are retained 30 days. For enterprise pilots we can extend searchable audit logs to 90 days and enable token-level tracing. Where feasible, we will scope caches so session caches expire within 24 hours for PHI endpoints.

Breach notification: our standard incident practice is to notify "as soon as reasonably possible." For enterprise agreements we can commit to an initial notification within 48 hours for confirmed incidents that affect confidential customer data, plus daily updates until resolution. If MedSys requires 72 hours instead, we can accept that as well; we prefer an explicit SLA in the DPA so expectations are aligned.

Next steps I propose:
- Redwood to upload an editable DPA redline (we can use DocuSign or a shared Google Doc).
- Security sync (30m) to show the dataflow and logging configuration; Marissa to schedule.
- Procurement: exchange subprocessor export and SOC2 snapshot. I attached SOC2_ROADMAP_2026.pdf with timing on the next audit window.

Attachments: SOC2_ROADMAP_2026.pdf

If you confirm residency and breach-notify SLA preference (48h vs 72h) we'll prepare the DPA redline focused on these enterprise controls.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0142

From: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@medsys.io>

Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up — privacy/dataflow questions & proposed next steps

Thanks Ben — that addresses most of our questions. A couple of quick confirmations from procurement/security here at MedSys: 

- Residency: confirmed EU-only required for pilot. Please ensure any subprocessor handling PHI is also EU-resident or subject to an EU-approved transfer mechanism.
- Breach: we will accept 48h initial notification if Redwood will commit contractually to that SLA; otherwise 72h will be our fallback. Prefer to lock to 48h for this account given the sensitivity.
- Cache behavior: please provide the specific config option name to disable persistent indexing for the PHI endpoints so our engineers can validate during the pilot.

I'm attaching a short diagram our infra team created (Prod-Privacy-Flow.pdf) which highlights the PHI boundaries — see top right note about "no long-term indexing of raw narrative data".

Marissa/Vivek — can we do a 30m call tomorrow (11/23) 09:00 CET to finalize MAP and agree on the DPA workflow? If you prefer, share a DocuSign envelope and we'll circulate internally.
